at falde.explanation: "At falde" means "to fall", for example to fall down, or for rain and snow to fall. Jeg faldt af cyklen means "I fell off the bike".

sentence.en: You can fall off the chair.

at finde.explanation: "At finde" means "to find", whether you look for something or come across it: Jeg finder mine nøgler (I find my keys). It is also used for opinions: Jeg finder det svært (I find it difficult).

sentence.en: I can't find my keys.

at flytte.explanation: "At flytte" means "to move", either to a new home or to shift something from one place to another. Vi flytter til Aarhus means "We are moving to Aarhus", and "Kan du flytte bilen?" means "Can you move the car?".

sentence.da: Vi skal **flytte** til et nyt hus.
sentence.en: We are going to move to a new house.

at flyve.explanation: "At flyve" means "to fly", for birds and for people travelling by plane: Vi flyver til Spanien (We are flying to Spain).

sentence.en: The bird can fly high.

at forhandle.explanation: "At forhandle" means "to negotiate", for example prices, contracts or pay. You negotiate about something with om (about): forhandle om prisen (negotiate the price). Be careful: en forhandler is not a negotiator but a dealer or retailer, such as a car dealer.

sentence.en: We want to negotiate the price.

at forklare.explanation: "At forklare" means "to explain". Danish says forklare noget for nogen (explain something to someone): Kan du forklare det for mig? (Can you explain it to me?).

sentence.en: The teacher will explain the word.

at forstå.explanation: "At forstå" means "to understand": Jeg forstår ikke (I don't understand). To say you know a fact, use at vide (to know) instead: Jeg ved det ikke (I don't know).

sentence.en: I cannot understand him.

at fortælle.explanation: "At fortælle" means "to tell", especially to tell a story or give someone information: Hun fortæller en historie (She tells a story). For simply saying a few words, use at sige (to say): Han siger hej (He says hello). You can add who you tell: fortælle nogen noget (tell someone something).

sentence.da: Min mormor vil **fortælle** en historie til børnene.
sentence.en: My grandmother will tell the children a story.

at fryse.explanation: "At fryse" means "to freeze" and also "to feel cold". Jeg fryser means I am cold (literally I freeze). It also describes water or food turning to ice. Do not mix it up with en fryser (a freezer).

sentence.en: Without a jacket you will freeze.

at fylde år.explanation: "At fylde år" means "to have a birthday", in the sense of turning a certain age. You can add the age: Jeg fylder tredive år (I am turning thirty). At have fødselsdag (to have a birthday) just says it is your birthday, without the age.

sentence.da: Min far skal **fylde år** i morgen.
sentence.en: My dad is having a birthday tomorrow.

at få.explanation: "At få" means "to get" or "to receive": Jeg får en gave (I get a present). It also appears in få lov (to be allowed): Jeg fik lov (I was allowed). It does not mean to go and fetch something. That is at hente (to fetch).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **få** en gave til min fødselsdag.
sentence.en: I am going to get a present for my birthday.

at få hjælp.explanation: "At få hjælp" means "to get help": Kan jeg få hjælp? (Can I get help?). Danish says hjælp (help) with no en (a) in front: Jeg har brug for hjælp (I need help).

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og vil **få hjælp**.
sentence.en: I am sick and want to get help.

at føle.explanation: "At føle" means "to feel", both emotions and things you touch. To say how you feel, add mig (me): Jeg føler mig glad means "I feel happy".

sentence.da: Jeg kan **føle** mig glad i dag.
sentence.en: I can feel happy today.

en familie.explanation: "En familie" means "a family": Har du en stor familie? (Do you have a big family?).

sentence.da: Min **familie** er mor, far og søster.
sentence.en: My family is mom, dad and sister.

en far.explanation: "En far" means "a father". You can also call him far directly: Hej, far! (Hi, Dad!).

sentence.da: Min mor og min **far** har to børn.
sentence.en: My mother and my father have two children.

en farfar.explanation: "En farfar" means "a grandfather" on your father's side. It is built from far (father) and far (father): father's father. On your mother's side he is en morfar (mother's father).

sentence.en: My grandfather is my father's father.

en farmor.explanation: "En farmor" means "a grandmother" on your father's side. It is built from far (father) and mor (mother): father's mother. You can call her farmor directly: Farmor kommer i dag (Grandma is coming today).

sentence.en: My grandmother is my father's mother.

en farve.explanation: "En farve" means "a color". In a shop you can ask Har I den i en anden farve? (Do you have it in another color?).

sentence.da: Hvilken **farve** har din bil? Den er rød.
sentence.en: What color is your car? It is red.

en feber.explanation: "En feber" means "a fever", a high body temperature when you are sick. Danes say Jeg har feber (I have a fever), usually without en.

sentence.da: Hun har **feber** og bliver i sengen.
sentence.en: She has a fever and stays in bed.

en ferie.explanation: "En ferie" means "a vacation" or holiday, a time away from work or school. You say på ferie (on vacation): Jeg er på ferie (I am on vacation). I ferien means "during the vacation".

sentence.da: Jeg har fri og tager på **ferie**.
sentence.en: I am off and going on vacation.

en fest.explanation: "En fest" means "a party" or a celebration. You say at holde fest (to have a party) or at gå til fest (to go to a party). God fest! means "Have a good party!".

sentence.da: Vi holder **fest** med musik og kage.
sentence.en: We are having a party with music and cake.

en film.explanation: "En film" means "a film" or "a movie". More than one is also "film": to film means two films (to is the number two). At se en film means "to watch a film".

sentence.en: We watch a film at the cinema.

en finger.explanation: "En finger" means "a finger". The thumb is tommelfinger and the index finger is pegefinger. Danish says the finger where English says my finger: Jeg har ondt i fingeren means "I have a pain in the finger", i.e. my finger hurts.

sentence.da: Hun har en ring på sin **finger**.
sentence.en: She has a ring on her finger.

en fisk.explanation: "En fisk" means "a fish", both the animal in the water and the food on your plate. The plural can be the same word as the single one: tre fisk (three fish).

sentence.en: A fish swims in the water.

en flaske.explanation: "En flaske" means "a bottle". Danish has no word for "of" here: en flaske vand is a bottle of water, and "et glas vand" is a glass of water.

sentence.da: Han hælder mælk fra en **flaske** i glasset.
sentence.en: He pours milk from a bottle into the glass.

en flybillet.explanation: "En flybillet" means "a plane ticket". It is built from fly (plane) and billet (ticket).

sentence.en: I have a plane ticket to Paris.

en fod.explanation: "En fod" means "a foot". Til fods means on foot (walking). Danish often says the feet where English says my feet: Jeg har ondt i fødderne means my feet hurt (literally I have a pain in the feet).

sentence.en: I have a pain in my foot.

en forfader.explanation: "En forfader" means "an ancestor", a family member who lived long ago. One step back from your grandparents is en oldefar (a great-grandfather).

sentence.da: Min **forfader** boede her for længe siden.
sentence.en: My ancestor lived here long ago.

en forkølelse.explanation: "En forkølelse" means "a cold", the illness with a runny nose and a sore throat. In everyday talk Danes more often say Jeg er forkølet (I have a cold). Do not mix it up with kold (cold in temperature).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **forkølelse** og ondt i halsen.
sentence.en: I have a cold and a sore throat.

en fornyelse.explanation: "En fornyelse" means "a renewal". It comes from at forny (to renew). You say en fornyelse af mit pas (a renewal of my passport).

sentence.da: Jeg skal have en **fornyelse** af mit pas.
sentence.en: I need a renewal of my passport.

en forret.explanation: "En forret" means "a starter", the small dish you eat before the main one. On a menu you say til forret (as a starter): Til forret tager jeg suppe means "As a starter I will have soup".

sentence.en: I will have soup as a starter.

en forsinkelse.explanation: "En forsinkelse" means "a delay". To say something is late, use forsinket: Toget er forsinket (The train is late).

sentence.da: Toget har en **forsinkelse** på en time.
sentence.en: The train has a delay of one hour.

en frakke.explanation: "En frakke" means "a coat". It is longer and warmer than en jakke (a jacket). At tage frakken på means "to put the coat on".

sentence.da: Jeg tager min **frakke** på i kulden.
sentence.en: I put my coat on in the cold.

en frikadelle.explanation: "En frikadelle" means "a meatball", a fried patty of minced meat.

sentence.da: Han steger en **frikadelle** af svinekød i panden.
sentence.en: He fries a meatball of pork in the pan.

en frisør.explanation: "En frisør" means "a hairdresser", and it also means the place where you get a haircut: Jeg har tid hos frisøren means "I have an appointment at the hairdresser's". A barber, who cuts men's hair, is en barber.

sentence.en: I am going to the hairdresser tomorrow.

en frugt.explanation: "En frugt" means "a fruit". For fruit in general Danes usually leave out en: Jeg spiser meget frugt (I eat a lot of fruit). One piece of fruit is et stykke frugt.

sentence.en: Apples and bananas are fruit.

en fugl.explanation: "En fugl" means "a bird". Fuglene synger means "The birds are singing", and en fugl kan flyve means "a bird can fly".

sentence.da: Der sidder en **fugl** i træet og synger.
sentence.en: A bird is sitting in the tree and singing.

en fætter.explanation: "En fætter" means "a male cousin", the son of your aunt or uncle. Danish has a separate word for a female cousin, en kusine, while English uses cousin for both.

sentence.da: Min **fætter** er søn af min mors bror.
sentence.en: My cousin is the son of my mother's brother.

en fødselsdag.explanation: "En fødselsdag" means "a birthday". The usual greeting is Tillykke med fødselsdagen! (Happy birthday!). Danes say Jeg har fødselsdag (literally I have birthday) where English says It is my birthday.

sentence.da: I dag har jeg **fødselsdag** og får kage.
sentence.en: Today it is my birthday and I get cake.

en fødselsdagsfest.explanation: "En fødselsdagsfest" means "a birthday party". It is built from fødselsdag (birthday) and fest (party).

sentence.da: Vi har **fødselsdagsfest** med kage og gaver.
sentence.en: We have a birthday party with cake and presents.

en fødselsdagsgave.explanation: "En fødselsdagsgave" means "a birthday present". It is built from fødselsdag (birthday) and gave (gift).

sentence.da: Jeg køber en **fødselsdagsgave** til min mor.
sentence.en: I am buying a birthday present for my mother.

en fødselsdato.explanation: "En fødselsdato" means "a date of birth", the day, month and year you were born. It is not the same as en fødselsdag (a birthday), the day you celebrate each year.

sentence.en: My date of birth is 12 March 1990.

et fly.explanation: "Et fly" means "a plane". En flyvemaskine (an airplane) also exists, but it is longer and et fly is the everyday word.

sentence.da: Vi sidder i et **fly** over skyerne.
sentence.en: We are sitting in a plane above the clouds.

et fornavn.explanation: "Et fornavn" means "a first name", the name you are given at birth, before the family name. It is made of for (before) and et navn (a name).

sentence.en: My first name is Anna.

et forår.explanation: "Et forår" means "a spring", the season between winter and summer when the flowers come out. Om foråret blomstrer træerne means "In spring the trees blossom".

sentence.en: It is spring with many flowers.

et får.explanation: "Et får" means "a sheep". Do not mix it up with får from at få (to get): Han får en gave means "He gets a gift".

sentence.da: Et **får** har uld og siger mæh.
sentence.en: A sheep has wool and says baa.

et fødested.explanation: "Et fødested" means "a birthplace", the town or country where someone was born. It is made of at føde (to give birth) and et sted (a place).

sentence.en: My birthplace is Odense.

faktisk.explanation: "Faktisk" means "actually" or "in fact". Use it when the truth is a bit different from what someone thinks: Jeg er faktisk dansk (I am actually Danish).

sentence.en: No, he is actually Danish.

fantastisk.explanation: "Fantastisk" means "fantastic". It is stronger than god (good), so save it for something really great.

sentence.en: The food was fantastic!

farlig.explanation: "Farlig" means "dangerous" and comes from fare (danger). Livsfarlig means "life-threatening".

sentence.en: The road is very dangerous.

farvel.explanation: "Farvel" means "goodbye". Danes often use hej hej (bye bye) or vi ses (see you) for everyday goodbyes, while farvel sounds more final.

sentence.en: I say goodbye to my friend.

fattig.explanation: "Fattig" means "poor", with little money, for people and also for countries. Stakkels also means "poor", but in the sense of unlucky: stakkels dig means "poor you".

sentence.da: Han er **fattig** og har næsten ingen penge.
sentence.en: He is poor and has almost no money.

februar.explanation: "Februar" means "February". Month names are written with a small letter: i februar (in February).

sentence.en: After January comes February.

fem.explanation: "Fem" means "five": fem fingre (five fingers). Fifty is not "femti" but halvtreds (fifty).

sentence.da: Jeg har **fem** fingre på hver hånd.
sentence.en: I have five fingers on each hand.

femogtredive.explanation: "Femogtredive" means "thirty-five". Danish says the five first: fem-og-tredive is literally five-and-thirty. The same goes for 25, femogtyve (five-and-twenty), and 45, femogfyrre (five-and-forty).

sentence.en: My brother is thirty-five years old.

femte.explanation: "Femte" means "fifth" and is used for order and dates: den femte marts (the fifth of March). Fem is the plain number: fem dage (five days), but den femte dag (the fifth day).

sentence.en: My birthday is the fifth of March.

femten.explanation: "Femten" means "fifteen": Jeg kommer om femten minutter (I am coming in fifteen minutes). Danes also say en kvart (a quarter of an hour) for fifteen minutes.

sentence.en: There are fifteen students in the class.

fin.explanation: "Fin" means "fine" or "nice". It can also mean "fancy" or "elegant": en fin restaurant means "a fancy restaurant". Fint! on its own means "Great!" or "Okay, good!".

sentence.en: The sun shines on a nice day.

finland.explanation: "Finland" means "Finland": Jeg bor i Finland (I live in Finland).

sentence.en: I come from Finland.

finsk.explanation: "Finsk" means "Finnish" and describes things from Finland, including the language. It is written with a small letter, even for the language: Jeg taler finsk means "I speak Finnish".

sentence.da: Han kommer fra Finland og taler **finsk**.
sentence.en: He comes from Finland and speaks Finnish.

fint.explanation: "Fint" means "fine" or "nicely". It is a common answer to Hvordan går det? (How is it going?): Det går fint (It is going fine). Alone, Fint! means "Fine!" and agrees with a plan: Skal vi mødes klokken tre? Fint! (Shall we meet at three? Fine!).

sentence.en: How is it going? It is going fine.

fire.explanation: "Fire" means "four": fire kroner (four kroner). Don't mix it up with fyrre (forty), which looks similar: fyrre kroner (forty kroner).

sentence.en: The dog has four legs.

fireogtyve.explanation: "Fireogtyve" means "twenty-four". Danish says the four first: fire-og-tyve is literally four-and-twenty. The same goes for 25, femogtyve (five-and-twenty), and 26, seksogtyve (six-and-twenty).

sentence.da: Der er **fireogtyve** timer i et døgn.
sentence.en: There are twenty-four hours in a day.

firs.explanation: "Firs" means "eighty": firs kroner (eighty kroner). It is short for firsindstyve (four times twenty). Sixty works the same way: tres (sixty) is three twenties.

sentence.en: My grandfather is eighty years old.

fjerde.explanation: "Fjerde" means "fourth" and is used for order and dates: den fjerde maj (the fourth of May). Fire is the plain number: fire dage (four days), but den fjerde dag (the fourth day).

sentence.en: He sat in the fourth row.

fjorten.explanation: "Fjorten" means "fourteen": fjorten børn (fourteen children). Danes say fjorten dage (fourteen days) for "two weeks": Vi ses om fjorten dage (See you in two weeks).

sentence.da: Vi tager på ferie i **fjorten** dage.
sentence.en: We are going on holiday for fourteen days (two weeks).

flere.explanation: "Flere" means "more" or "several", for things you can count one by one: Jeg vil have flere kager (I want more cakes). For something you can't count, use mere: Jeg vil have mere kage (I want more cake), mere vand (more water).

sentence.en: We have several cars in the garage.

flot.explanation: "Flot" means "good-looking" or "impressive", for people, clothes, places and even results. Saying Flot! to someone means "Well done!".

sentence.da: Hun er smuk og har en **flot** kjole.
sentence.en: She is beautiful and has a nice-looking dress.

fløde.explanation: "Fløde" means "cream". Piskefløde means "whipping cream" and is made of piske (to whip) and "fløde".

sentence.en: Do you want cream in your coffee?

fodbold.explanation: "Fodbold" means "soccer". The game has no en in front: Jeg spiller fodbold means "I play soccer". En fodbold is the ball.

sentence.da: Børnene spiller **fodbold** og sparker til bolden.
sentence.en: The children play soccer and kick the ball.

for.explanation: "For" means "for", too or "ago", depending on the sentence. Compare Suppen er varm (The soup is hot) with Suppen er for varm (The soup is too hot). With siden (ago) it counts back in time: for to dage siden (two days ago). For a gift, Danish usually says til: en gave til dig (a gift for you).

sentence.en: The soup is too hot.

for eksempel.explanation: "For eksempel" means "for example". It goes right before the example: Jeg spiser meget frugt, for eksempel bananer (I eat a lot of fruit, for example bananas). In writing it is often shortened to fx (e.g.).

forms.da: Jeg kan godt lide frugt, for eksempel æbler.
forms.en: I like fruit, for example apples.

forms.da: Vi kan mødes, for eksempel i morgen.
forms.en: We can meet, for example tomorrow.

sentence.en: I eat fruit, for example apples.

for pokker.explanation: "For pokker" means "darn it" or "for heaven's sake". It is a mild thing to say when something annoying or surprising happens.

forms.da: For pokker, jeg har glemt nøglen!
forms.en: Darn it, I forgot the key!

sentence.en: Darn it, I forgot the key!

foran.explanation: "Foran" means "in front of". Compare Jeg står foran døren (I stand in front of the door) with Jeg står bag døren (I stand behind the door). Før (before) is only for time, not place: før klokken fem (before five o'clock).

sentence.en: The car is parked in front of the house.

forbi.explanation: "Forbi" means "past" or "by". Han gik forbi huset means He walked past the house (he did not stop). It also means "over": Sommeren er forbi (The summer is over). Kom forbi i aften! means "Drop by tonight!".

sentence.en: The bus drives past the school.

fordi.explanation: "Fordi" means "because". It answers Hvorfor? (Why?): Hvorfor er du træt? (Why are you tired?) - Fordi jeg sover for lidt (Because I sleep too little). Do not mix it up with derfor (that is why): Jeg er træt, derfor går jeg i seng (I am tired, that is why I go to bed).

sentence.da: Jeg bliver hjemme **fordi** jeg er syg.
sentence.en: I stay home because I am sick.

forkert.explanation: "Forkert" means "wrong" or "incorrect", for answers, directions, numbers or choices. To say you made a mistake, say Jeg tog fejl (I was mistaken).

sentence.da: Fem plus fem er tolv. Det er **forkert**.
sentence.en: Five plus five is twelve. That is wrong.

forkølet.explanation: "Forkølet" means "having a cold". Jeg er forkølet means "I have a cold". It is milder than syg (sick).

sentence.en: I have a cold and cough a lot.

forsinket.explanation: "Forsinket" means "delayed" or "late", mostly for trains, buses and planes. About yourself you can also say Jeg er forsinket (I am late).

sentence.en: The train is delayed by twenty minutes.

fortroligt.explanation: "Fortroligt" means "confidentially" or "in confidence", for things you tell one person who must keep them to themselves: Jeg fortæller dig det fortroligt (I am telling you this in confidence). It also means "confidential": Dokumentet er fortroligt (The document is confidential).

forms.en: I am telling you this in confidence

sentence.da: Det er **fortroligt**. Sig det ikke til andre.
sentence.en: It is confidential. Do not tell anyone else.

forældre.explanation: "Forældre" means "parents", mother and father together. For just one parent, say en forælder (a parent).

sentence.da: Min mor og min far er mine **forældre**.
sentence.en: My mom and my dad are my parents.

fra.explanation: "Fra" means "from". It works for places, people and times: Jeg er fra Danmark (I am from Denmark), fra mandag til fredag (from Monday to Friday). Compare en gave til mig (a gift for me) with en gave fra mig (a gift from me).

sentence.en: The train goes from Copenhagen to Aarhus.

frankrig.explanation: "Frankrig" means "France": Jeg bor i Frankrig (I live in France).

sentence.en: Paris is in France.

fransk.explanation: "Fransk" means "French", for things from France and for the language. It is written with a small letter: Jeg taler fransk (I speak French).

sentence.da: Hun kommer fra Frankrig og taler **fransk**.
sentence.en: She comes from France and speaks French.

franskbrød.explanation: "Et franskbrød" means "a white loaf", the ordinary light kind. It is made of fransk (French) and brød (bread). Rugbrød (rye bread) is the dark, heavy kind.

sentence.en: I buy a white loaf at the baker's.

fredag.explanation: "Fredag" means "Friday". På fredag means on Friday (the coming one) and "om fredagen" means on Fridays (every Friday). Day names are written with a small letter.

sentence.en: After Thursday comes Friday.

fri.explanation: "Fri" means "free" and also "off" from work or school: Jeg har fri means "I am off work". It does not mean free of charge; for that use gratis.

sentence.da: I dag har jeg **fri** fra arbejde.
sentence.en: Today I am off from work.

frisk.explanation: "Frisk" means "fresh", for food and air. For a person it means "healthy": Jeg er frisk means "I am well".

sentence.da: Jeg købte mælken i dag. Den er **frisk**.
sentence.en: I bought the milk today. It is fresh.

fritid.explanation: "Fritid" means "free time", the time when you are not at work or school. You say Jeg har ikke meget fritid (I do not have much free time).

sentence.en: In my free time I go for walks.

frokost.explanation: "Frokost" means "lunch", the meal around midday. Hvad skal vi have til frokost? means "What are we having for lunch?".

sentence.en: It is twelve o'clock. We eat lunch.

frossen.explanation: "Frossen" means "frozen", food that has been kept so cold that it is hard. For a person who feels cold, do not use it: Danes say jeg fryser (I am cold, literally I freeze).

sentence.en: The pizza in the freezer is frozen.

fuld.explanation: "Fuld" means "full", for a glass, a bus or a room. When it describes a person, it means "drunk": Han er fuld means "He is drunk". To say you are full after a meal, use mæt (full after eating).

sentence.en: The bus is completely full of people.

fyrre.explanation: "Fyrre" means "forty". Do not mix it up with fire (four): fire kroner is four kroner, fyrre kroner is forty kroner. For 41 you say enogfyrre, literally one-and-forty.

sentence.en: I am forty years old.

færdig.explanation: "Færdig" means "finished" or "done", for example after a meal or at the end of work. Do not mix it up with klar (ready), which means prepared to start: Er du klar? (Are you ready?).

sentence.da: Jeg har skrevet brevet. Nu er jeg **færdig**.
sentence.en: I have written the letter. Now I am done.

færdig med.explanation: "Færdig med" means "finished with". After med (with) you put the thing (færdig med lektierne, finished with the homework) or an action starting with at (færdig med at spise, finished eating).

forms.en: Are you finished with the book?

forms.da: Vi er færdige med at spise.

sentence.en: Now I am finished with work.

før.explanation: "Før" means "before" in time. Jeg kommer før klokken fem (I come before five o'clock), Jeg spiser, før du kommer (I eat before you come). For place, use foran (in front of): foran huset (in front of the house).

sentence.en: Four o'clock is before five o'clock.

først.explanation: "Først" means "first" or "not until". Først spiser vi, så går vi (First we eat, then we go). Jeg kommer først i morgen means "I am not coming until tomorrow". Do not mix it up with første (the first one): den første dag (the first day).

sentence.en: We eat first and go afterwards.

første.explanation: "Første" means "first" in a list or order. It is used in dates: den første maj (the first of May), written 1. maj. Do not mix it up with først, which tells when something happens: Først spiser vi (First we eat).

sentence.en: Today is my first day.
